# Cwift.net

> Cwift.net is the minimal, first-person site for Brian Ward's 24-hour desktop appraisals of California homes and condominiums. Brian Ward is a California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser (license AR036053) who has appraised California homes since 2004. Reports are emailed within 24 hours of payment and photos, seven days a week. Same appraiser and service as cwift.com; standard-schedule reports are also offered by date-of-death.com.

## Facts
- Within 24 hours: Standard Desktop $675, Basic Desktop $450
- Regular schedule (5–10 business days): Standard $449, Basic $299
- The 24 hours start once payment and photos have both arrived; weekends and holidays count
- Coverage: all of California, every county and ZIP code (207 county, city and neighborhood pages at https://www.cwift.net/areas); single-family homes, condominiums and townhomes (not 2–4 units, apartments, commercial or land); not for loans
- Also called: a virtual, remote or online appraisal; it is a full appraisal by a licensed appraiser without a site visit
- Contact: contact@cwift.net or https://www.cwift.net/order. No phone number by design: email and online submission are the fastest way to get service
- Statement: I've prepared desktop appraisals for every purpose on this list. Some situations still call for an in-person appraisal, though, so check with your attorney or tax advisor first to make sure a desktop report is right for yours.

## Uses (date of death first)
- [Date of death & step-up in basis](https://www.cwift.net/uses#date-of-death): Heirs usually receive a fresh tax basis equal to the home's value on the day the owner died. The appraisal pins down that figure, so capital gains are calculated correctly when the house sells, even if the death was years ago.
- [Trusts & estates](https://www.cwift.net/uses#trust-estate): Trustees and executors need a value they can defend: for an accounting, for dividing things fairly, or for selling the house to one of the beneficiaries. A signed appraisal answers the question of where the number came from.
- [Divorce & separation](https://www.cwift.net/uses#divorce): Whether one of you keeps the house or it gets sold, settlement talks move faster with an independent value. I can value the home as of today, the date of separation, or both.
- [Family sales & buyouts](https://www.cwift.net/uses#family-transfers): Buying out a brother's share, selling to your daughter, or splitting a house with a former partner? The appraisal gives everyone the same starting point and records a fair price.
- [Gift tax](https://www.cwift.net/uses#gift-tax): Deeding a house, or part of one, to a relative is a gift with a value that gets reported. The appraisal supports the figure on the federal gift-tax return, Form 709.
- [Prop 19 transfers](https://www.cwift.net/uses#prop-19): When a parent's home passes to a child, Prop 19 limits how much of the old assessment carries over. Market value on the transfer date shows where you stand with the county assessor.
- [Property tax appeals](https://www.cwift.net/uses#property-tax-appeal): If the county assesses your home above what it would sell for, an independent appraisal is the evidence for a decline-in-value review or a formal appeal.
- [Bankruptcy](https://www.cwift.net/uses#bankruptcy): Your attorney needs a supportable value for the schedules and the homestead exemption. Problems with the house get documented from your photos, so they count.
- [Before you sell](https://www.cwift.net/uses#pre-listing): Set the asking price with an opinion from someone who isn't trying to win your listing.
- [Before you buy](https://www.cwift.net/uses#pre-purchase): Paying cash, buying from family, or skipping the appraisal contingency? Check the price while you can still walk away.
- [Immigration sponsors (I-864)](https://www.cwift.net/uses#immigration): Sponsors who count home equity on the Affidavit of Support are asked for a recent appraisal by a licensed appraiser. This is that appraisal.
- [Bail & property bonds](https://www.cwift.net/uses#bail-bonds): Courts that take a property bond want proof of the equity, usually from a licensed appraiser. A current report keeps the bond paperwork moving.
